core_claims.name: Raw / HasType
core_claims.scope: Externally typed, intrinsically scoped simple lambda calculus with natural numbers, case, and general fixpoints; arbitrary finite scopes and context vectors. Scope does not imply typability.

core_claims.name: rename / subst / instantiate
core_claims.scope: Capture-avoiding raw renaming and simultaneous substitution between arbitrary scopes, extended under lambda, successor-case, and fixpoint binders. Substitution itself accepts arbitrary open arguments.

core_claims.name: Step / Steps
core_claims.scope: Weak left-to-right call-by-value reduction on all Raw n terms, including ill-typed terms, with value-restricted lambda and successor-case beta and unrestricted fixpoint unfolding; finite reflexive-transitive closure.

core_claims.name: appendSteps / applicationSteps
core_claims.scope: Composition of arbitrary finite traces and lifting through the function position of application, at every scope.

core_claims.name: numeralValue / numeralType / identityType / plusType / multiplyType / churchTwoType / constantType
core_claims.scope: General numeral value/typing proofs and actual derivations for identity, recursive addition/multiplication, Church two, and the constant function in arbitrary contexts.

core_claims.name: identityTwo / nestedIdentity / zeroApplicationUntypable
core_claims.scope: Concrete one- and two-step CBV identity traces; impossibility of assigning any result type to closed zero-applied-to-zero.

exercises.scope: Two-step nested-identity trace that uses AppR before outer Beta.
Encoding and typing of the constant function, retaining the older variable under a binder.
No external typing of closed zero applied to zero, for any requested type.

deviations: Named variables are replaced from the outset by Fin-scoped raw syntax and Vect contexts. Named shadowing is explained as de Bruijn positions; no string-name resolver is provided.
Typing remains external in Lambda and Properties, so ill-typed scoped terms remain representable and the preservation theorem is a separate proof.
Capture-avoiding substitution supports arbitrary open arguments rather than relying on closed replacements in the named presentation.
Pedagogical exercises are adapted to the scoped representation; not every alternative-presentation or Church-arithmetic exercise from upstream is reproduced.
